drills.coachNote: Black wanted exactly what he got: his queen on c6 sits on the c6-e4 diagonal, and since your pawn on e3 cuts the defense your queen on e2 would normally give, the knight on e4 was simply undefended. Rac1 developed a rook but did nothing about that, so Qxe4 just won the piece clean, and Black followed up with c4, f5, c5 to consolidate the extra material (eval swing 4.5). The move was Nd2, retreating the knight to safety before anything else; play continues normally with Rd8, Nf3, Kg7, Qc2, Rd6. Before any natural developing move, scan for anything of yours already hanging — a new move doesn't fix an old problem unless it's aimed at it.
drills.threat: Your knight on e4 is attacked by Black's queen on c6, and your own pawn on e3 is blocking your queen from defending it.
